title: [Feature Request] Undo branches
description:
Undo branches / undo tree allows you to undo some changes,
then make a new change, while keeping all changes available in the undo tree.
The undo tree can therefore prevent awkward scenarios such as:
 * Losing all redo futures by accidentally pressing a button during undo
 * Copying the file or save it with git when trying multiple alternatives

This screen-cap showcases how it works in Emacs with undo-tree.



https://github.com/someone/vscode/commit/c5699711d21dece88c7c608f6d8ae277f72a0081 contains the changes to the model that are needed, but several questions remain to be answered. I'm interested in completing the feature but need further input before proceeding.
* How should the UI look? Graphics / ASCII, clickable?
* Should the tree be formatted like in Emacs undo-tree (as short tree as possible) or like Vim's Gundo http://screenr.com/M9l (one state per line sorted by time)?
* What unit-tests should be added?

You can try out the current changes by compiling my fork and you'll find 'History Tree' in the Edit menu. Clicking the menu item will console.log a function that changes what redo future is selected (just like in the gif).

title: Language services should be able to provide debug console IntelliSense
description:
### Scenario
Currently, debug adapters can provide IntelliSense in the console. This is great for untyped or weakly typed languages like JavaScript/TypeScript. But for statically typed languages, such as C#, the best way to do this is to let the regular language service provide IntelliSense just like in the editor.

### Basic proposal
In the language service registration for an extension, a language service can indicate that it supports debug console IntelliSense. If the language of the document of the current stack frame opts into this, then instead of going down the path where completion is requested from debug adapter, it is instead requested from the language service. VS Code would need to provide the location of the active stack frame in the same way that regular intellisense works. Then it would need to provide the text and position of the line being edited in the debug console.

Assuming that VS Code is eventually interested in supporting this, https://github.com/someone/omnisharp-vscode/issues/1609 tracks the work in the C# extension to support this.

title: Dictation support for visual studio code
description:
Hi, 

I wish to lodge a request to have VS Code updated so that it can accept dictation input. Currently, if you try to dictate into VS Code using software like Dragon (the industry standard), nothing happens. 

This is important to fix for people like myself who have long term hand injuries and are trying to figure out ways to program by voice. People have managed programming by voice in these situations, but the solutions are difficult to develop and not pretty. 

To be clear, I'm not asking that you develop voice commands to input symbols by voice, only that the text boxes in VS Code (and/or Visual Studio) can accept dictation input by Dragon (preferably with full 'select-and-say' support). Voice programmers can take care of the rest. 

Does it have to be Dragon? Not necessarily. It could be any local speech recognition engine with good accuracy (I'd argue that the decade old Windows Voice Recognition isn't quite there yet) and the ability to write custom voice commands. 

While there are few people using such technologies today, it is a subject of interest to all programmers, because they may need it in the future. 

- Jole

title: Support external diff algorithms in internal diff editor
description:
Reopening closed feature request an earlier issue

Openness, extensibility and customisability are the features that keep me coming back to VSCode. Being built upon an OSS core (Electron) was strong evidence of a change of culture at Microsoft. 

In that spirit, would you please reconsider the original request from @someone. Different diffing algorithms produce [significantly different results][1] and are suited to different purposes. There is no one-size-fits-all solution.

Paraphrasing @someone, **please consider abstracting the diff functionality to allow different *hunk-list providers***. Respecting [the algorithm set in Git configuration][2] would be an ideal baseline.

As another example, **BeyondCompare** allows [significant customisation][3], including 2 of the 4 algorithms offered by Git.

[1]: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10664-019-09772-z
[2]: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff#Documentation/git-diff.txt---diff-algorithmpatienceminimalhistogrammyers

title: Change undo/redo to time based, AKA allow undo without erasing redo
description:
Imagine you are programming something.
After some time you aren't sure of something, so you check an earlier version of it.
After some Ctrl-Zs you accidentally press a key, and that's it all of your unsaved code is gone.

If we treat the undo button as a rewind button, we can prevent this!
A) ----> Original changes
B) <---- Undoing them
C) --->  New changes
becomes linearly:

A) ----> B) ----> C) --->

Currently, whenever a key is pressed (changes to a webview are made) a new entry is pushed into the 'undo stack' and the 'redo stack' is emptied.
Instead, we can add the 'redo stack' to the  'undo stack' to keep 'alternate futures' of the webview.
Specifically, we will want the following whenever the 'undo stack' is populated:
'undo stack' = 'undo stack' + inverted 'redo stack' + 'redo stack' + new 'undo stack' entry (change)

Further reading:
https://github.com/someone/klonk/blob/master/TheGURQ.md

title: Switch back to previous application after "code --wait"
description:
When using `code --wait` in, for example, Terminal.app on Mac, it would be convenient if it would switch back to Terminal.app after closing the file in VS Code.

For now I'm approximating the behavior on Mac with a small wrapper script:
```
#/bin/sh

pid="$(osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get unix id of first process whose frontmost is true')"
code -w "$@"
osascript -e "tell application \"System Events\" to set frontmost of processes whose unix id is $pid to true"
```

title: Allow Queued/Steering Prompts for Copilot Agent Chat
description:
It would be useful to support queuing prompts for the Copilot Agent chat interface, where a second prompt can be submitted while the first is still running, and automatically processed once the current task completes.

### Why this matters:

There are many scenarios where you already know what your *next* prompt will be, but you have to wait until the agent finishes its current operation before you can submit it. This interrupts workflow and slows down the feedback loop.

This queuing feature would be especially helpful when the second prompt depends on the *result or code changes* made by the first. For example:

* I ask Copilot to refactor a block of code.
* I already know I want to generate a related unit test after that refactor completes.
* Since the second prompt depends on the updated code, it's not something I can run in parallel via a second agent.
* Instead of waiting manually, I could queue the next prompt to be executed right after the first completes.

### Proposed behaviour:

* Allow a secondary prompt to be queued while a Copilot Agent is busy.
* It gets automatically submitted once the previous task finishes.
* (Optional) A visual indicator or prompt queue list would help keep track of what's pending.

This would improve usability without requiring parallel agents or manual timing.

title: Terminal auto-approve should parse shell command arguments for more granular trust
description:
The terminal's command approval feature doesn't inspect the arguments passed to shell executables like `pwsh.exe`, `bash`, etc. When GitHub Copilot suggests a command that wraps an actual command in a shell-invoking syntax (e.g., `pwsh.exe -Command "dotnet test path_to_csproj"`), the approval mechanism only recognizes `pwsh.exe` as the command, not the `dotnet test` part inside the string.

This leads to a poor user experience and a potential security issue. To use the auto-approve feature effectively, the user is forced to add the shell executable itself (e.g., `pwsh.exe`) to the allowed list. This effectively disables the security check for *any* command executed through that shell, undermining the purpose of the feature.

The desired behavior would be for the approval system to be intelligent enough to parse the command line, identify the actual command being executed within the shell's argument, and check *that* command against the approval list.

1.  Add a specific, safe command to the list of approved commands in your settings. For example, add `dotnet test` to `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove`.
2.  Have Copilot execute a command in the following format:
    ```powershell
    pwsh.exe -Command "dotnet test C:/proj/proj.csproj"
    ```

#### **Expected Behavior**

The command executes without a security prompt because the core command being run, `dotnet test`, is already on the approved list.

title: Increase the inter-session messaging limit beyond 50
description:
## Problem

The server currently allows only 50 messages between sessions. Complex multi-session workflows can hit this limit quickly, after which coordination messages are not delivered and the user must manually relay them between sessions.

The resulting message is similar to:

> Coordination limitation: session messaging reached its limit, so neither relay was delivered.

## Scenario

1. Query all CI failures from the last week and ask an agent to classify them.
2. Ask the agent to start sessions to fix the top 6-10 issues.
3. Many fixes have overlapping changes, so the sessions need to coordinate frequently.
4. The 50-message limit is reached before the work is complete, blocking further inter-session coordination.

## Request

Increase the number of server-side messages allowed between sessions from 50 to a meaningfully higher value so coordination-heavy workflows can complete without manual message relaying.

## Verification

1. Set `chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits` to `off` and start a new Agent Host session.
2. Ask the agent to create enough sessions/chats or send enough inter-session messages to reach the legacy limit.
3. Verify the limit is enforced with a clear error and rejected operations leave no partial session or chat.
4. Change the setting to `on` without reloading.
5. Repeat the orchestration workflow and verify the increased process-wide session, chat, and message limits apply live.

title: Feature: Support extraBody configuration for BYOK custom models
description:
## Summary

Allow BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) custom models to configure additional request body fields via an `extraBody` property in `chatLanguageModels.json`. This would enable users to pass model-specific parameters that are not currently supported through the existing `modelOptions` configuration.
(**This text was created with Copilot!**)

## Use Case

When using custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints (like vLLM, local inference servers, or specialized APIs), models often require additional parameters beyond the currently supported `temperature` and `top_p`:

- `reasoning_effort` (for reasoning models)
- `preserve_thinking` (to retain internal reasoning in responses)
- `chat_template_kwargs` (for custom chat template configuration)
- Provider-specific parameters for cache control, routing, or session management
- Custom model options (e.g., `output_config`, nested configuration objects)

```json

  "models": [

      "id": "GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",
      "name": "2xDGX-GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3",

      "maxInputTokens": 262144,

      "modelOptions": {

title: Allow TreeItem.command to declare an alternative command for modifier-click
description:
### Problem

A `TreeItem` can declare a single `command`, executed when the user clicks the item's label. There is no way to declare a different command for a modifier-click (Alt/Ctrl/Cmd), so extensions that expose a "primary action" and a closely-related variant must either pick one as the click behaviour, or ship a setting that flips it globally.

The common shape of this is "open" vs "open in a new window" / "open to the side": conventional in tabbed UIs, and something users expect to work by habit.

### Why this is a gap rather than a new concept

VS Code already has exactly this concept, one level down. The `menus` contribution point accepts an `alt` key, documented as the identifier of an alternative command to run, which must itself be declared in the `commands` section. So an inline action *button* on a tree item can already have an alt behaviour, while the tree item's own click cannot. The proposal is only to close that asymmetry.

### Proposal

Let `TreeItem.command` be paired with an optional alternative, e.g.:

```ts
treeItem.command = { command: 'ext.open', title: '', arguments: [x] };
treeItem.altCommand = { command: 'ext.openInNewWindow', title: '', arguments: [x] };
```

Semantics mirroring `menus.alt`: when the modifier is held at click time, the alternative runs instead. Extensions that don't set it are unaffected.

### Alternatives considered

- **A setting per extension.** Works, but it's a global flip rather than a per-click choice, and every extension r

description:
### Summary

Transition GitHub and Microsoft authentication used by agents to the host-owned authentication model proposed in [microsoft/agent-host-protocol#404](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/404).

### Current architecture

VS Code owns the authentication state and obtains credentials through its authentication providers, then brokers tokens to the agent host. This couples agent authentication to the VS Code client and extension host lifecycle.

### Desired architecture

- The agent host/runtime owns its GitHub and Microsoft account state and credentials.
- VS Code no longer retains authentication state solely to pass tokens into the agent host.
- When an interactive authentication flow is required, the host delegates client-specific UI operations such as opening a browser to VS Code through the Agent Host Protocol.
- Authentication state and flows follow the host-owned auth proposal while preserving an appropriate client-brokered path for sandboxed hosts.

### Scope

Focus initially on GitHub and Microsoft authentication, including account discovery, sign-in, sign-out, token refresh, and migration from the existing VS Code-owned token flow.

title: Voice Mode: record a categorized rejection reason for invalid confirmation narrations
description:
### Problem

When the voice backend rejects a confirmation narration with a `narration_ack` disposition of `invalid`, the client drops the narration and emits `voiceNarrationDropped` with `kind: 'confirmation'` and `reason: 'invalid'`. This identifies the outcome, but not why the backend rejected the request, making it difficult to diagnose confirmations that are not spoken.

`IVoiceNarrationAck` already includes an optional backend `reason`. `_handleNarrationAck` writes it to the local trace log but does not include a diagnostic category in telemetry.

### Proposed change

Preserve the existing `reason` field as the disposition/drop category, and add a separate bounded, categorized rejection-reason field to `voiceNarrationDropped` for invalid confirmation narrations.

- Define an allowlisted set of stable reason codes based on the backend contract. Coordinate a typed backend reason code if the current reason is free-form.
- Map missing or unrecognized reasons to explicit `missing`/`unknown` categories.
- Do not forward raw backend reason text, narration text, transcripts, session descriptions, or identifiers into the new field.
- Add the appropriate telemetry classification and document the new field's semantics.

- `false`: deactivate it for the repository.

- Ignore repository plugin settings until the workspace is trusted.

title: Explain enterprise minVersion restrictions in Chat, the Agents window, and a window-level banner
description:
Enterprise Managed Settings `minVersion` lets enterprise administrators block AI features on outdated VS Code clients until users update. For example, an organization can require a release with newer sandboxing protections.

Chat shows an update notice. The Editor also shows a grey Workspace Trust-style banner so users understand why AI is unavailable even when Chat is closed; other editor features remain usable. title: Terminal: support crisp font rendering on HiDPI displays
description:
Terminal text in VS Code looks noticeably softer than the same font in Ghostty and other native terminals on macOS HiDPI. I've heard this from a few people: the integrated terminal reads "dull" next to a standalone terminal at the same font and size.

I dug into it and the difference on macOS is the font antialiasing policy, not resolution. Editor and workbench text get one policy, terminal text on the GPU canvas path gets another, so terminal glyphs read heavier and blurrier.

Proposal: an opt-in `terminal.integrated.fontRendering` setting, `inherit` as the unchanged default and `crisp` as the opt-in mode, scoped to terminal text only so the editor, workbench, terminal theme, font family, size and weight don't change. On Windows and Linux the GPU renderer could request grayscale antialiasing through xterm's existing alpha-capable canvas path.

Comparison on macOS HiDPI, left `crisp`, right current:

It should apply to normal, detached and sticky-scroll terminals, and keep terminal image transparency working.

Upstream: xterm.js doesn't expose a font antialiasing option today, so VS Code has to go through the `allowTransparency` canvas path to get this. A dedicated antialiasing/font-rendering option in xterm.js (WebGL and DOM renderers) would let this be a first-class setting rather than a side effect, and would help every xterm.js embedder, not just VS Code. Until then this stays experimental, since the visible result depends on OS, display scale, font and theme.

title: Allow model- and agent-specific color indicators in Copilot Chat
description:
## Problem

In Copilot Chat I regularly switch between multiple agents and language models.
The currently selected agent and model are shown only as text, which makes it
easy to start a request with the wrong configuration in a compact chat UI.

VS Code theme colors can currently customize generic dropdown and menu states,
but they cannot assign a distinct visual identity to a specific agent or model.
For example, I would like to immediately distinguish "GPT-5.6 Sol" from "GPT-5.6 Luna" by
color, both in the selected controls and in the picker list.

## Requested feature

Add support for optional, user-configurable color indicators for individual
chat agents and language models.

The indicator could be a small colored dot, icon accent, border, or subtle
background in:

- the selected agent control
- the selected model control
- the agent/model picker list

This should use stable agent/model identifiers rather than display names, so
renaming a model does not break the configuration.

An API or setting could look conceptually like this:

```jsonc
{
  "chat.modelColorCustomizations": {
    "<stable-model-id>": "#f59e0b"
  },
  "chat.agentColorCustomizations": {
    "<stable-agent-id>": "#14b8a6"
  }
}

title: Automations: optionally skip a run while a previous session is still running
description:
## Feature request

Add an opt-in **skip if still running** option for automations. When a trigger fires and a session started by an earlier run of the same automation is still running, skip the new run instead of starting another session.

## Motivation

Scheduled or frequently triggered automations can overlap when a previous session takes longer than the trigger interval. Users should be able to prevent duplicate work and competing changes without having to monitor sessions manually.

## Expected behavior

- Make this configurable per automation; preserve the existing behavior when the option is disabled.
- When enabled, check whether a session from an earlier run of that automation is still running before starting another session.
- If so, skip this occurrence rather than queueing it or cancelling the existing session.
- Show the occurrence as skipped, with the reason that an earlier session is still running.
- Once the previous session has finished, subsequent triggers can start sessions normally.
- Apply the overlap guard atomically so simultaneous triggers cannot both start a session.

The precise definition of "still running" (including sessions waiting for user input or approval) should be documented as part of the design.

title: Automations: support script-first actions with optional AI continuation
description:

Allow an automation to start by executing a script, before creating an AI session. The script should be able to complete the automation entirely without AI participation, or request that a new AI session be started.

## Motivation

Many automations can do useful work with a script alone, or cheaply determine that there is nothing for an agent to do. Starting an AI session for every trigger adds unnecessary cost and noise. Conversely, a script may discover work or encounter a failure for which AI assistance is useful.

| Success | No | Complete the automation successfully without involving AI. |

| Failure | No | Report the failed script/run without involving AI. |
| Failure | Yes | Start a new AI session with the failure details for investigation or recovery; retain the script failure in the run history. |

## Expected behavior

title: Explore cross-platform pre-warming for agent worktrees
description:
## Motivation

Fresh worktree-isolated agent sessions currently defer worktree creation until the first send so the prompt can influence branch naming. That prevents the agent runtime and workspace-dependent caches from pre-warming, adding avoidable latency to the first turn.

We should investigate whether worktrees can be provisioned or prepared earlier without sacrificing naming quality, correctness, or cleanup guarantees across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Investigation

Explore a cross-platform design for pre-warming agent worktrees, including:

- When pre-warming can start and which inputs are available before the first prompt.
- Whether to create a provisional worktree/branch and rename it later, reserve a path, or split filesystem preparation from Git worktree creation.
- Coordination with Agent Host/runtime pre-warming so providers do not materialize against a pending or incorrect working directory.
- Cancellation, abandoned composers, restart recovery, stale provisional worktrees, and deterministic cleanup.
- Repository locking and races when multiple sessions pre-warm concurrently.
- Windows path-length, file-locking, antivirus, junction/symlink, and case-sensitivity behavior.
- macOS/Linux filesystem and symlink behavior, permissions, and performance differences.
- Interaction with trust, remote workspaces, multi-root workspaces, submodules, sparse checkout, LFS, and `git.worktreeIncludeFiles`.
- Disk usage and limits for speculative worktrees.

## Measurements

description:
## Summary

Add an explicit environment picker to the Agents Window new-session experience. Initially, the picker could offer **Local** and **Remote**, **Cloud** while being designed to accommodate additional environment types over time.

## Motivation

The place where work runs is a distinct choice from the source or workspace being used. Today these concepts can become coupled, making it harder to understand or extend session creation as more execution environments become available.

An environment picker would make this choice visible and establish a scalable model for environments such as:

- **Local** — run on the current machine.
- **Remote** — run through a supported remote connection or host.
- Future environments, such as cloud-hosted, containerized, or other provider-backed environments.

## Proposed direction

- Add an **Environment** picker to the new-session UI.
- Keep environment selection independent from:
  - Source/workspace selection.
  - Agent or harness selection.
  - Session intent.
- Start with **Local** and **Remote** where supported.
- Allow environment providers to contribute availability, display information, configuration/connection actions, and capability constraints without redesigning the picker for every new environment type

title: BYOK custom endpoints: support dynamic/refreshable API key (apiKeyHelper) for OAuth-based gateways
description:
### Feature request

The BYOK "custom endpoint" model configuration (`vendor: "customendpoint"`) only accepts a **static** credential in `apiKey` (or `requestHeaders`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`. There is no way to supply a **dynamically generated / short-lived** token.

This blocks any enterprise gateway that uses **OAuth** instead of static API keys, because OAuth access tokens are short-lived (e.g. ~1h) and must be refreshed. Today the only options are (a) manually pasting a fresh token every hour, or (b) running a local reverse-proxy that injects the token — both are poor workarounds for what should be first-class.

### Requested behavior

Add a way for the custom endpoint to obtain its credential dynamically per request, e.g.:

- An `apiKeyHelper`-style setting pointing to a local script/command whose stdout is the current token (same model as Claude Code's [`apiKeyHelper`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#credential-management)), and/or
- Support for `${env:VAR}` / secret references resolved at request time in `apiKey` / `requestHeaders`.

### Concrete use case

Authenticating against a **Databricks AI Gateway** (`/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions`) with OAuth (U2M) instead of a personal access token. The Databricks CLI already mints and auto-refreshes OAuth tokens (`databricks auth token`); an `apiKeyHelper` hook would let it feed the current token to VS Code transparently.

title: Add manual cleanup command for Agents Window worktrees
description:
## Feature request

Provide an **Agents: Clean Up Session Worktrees...** command so users can inspect and reclaim worktree storage without waiting for the automatic worktree-limit prompt.

## Proposed behavior

- Make the command available in the Agents Window when the experimental worktree cleanup feature is enabled.
- Show every safe cleanup candidate: completed, inactive, non-archived sessions that exclusively own their worktrees.
- Clearly explain why each row is or is not recommended:
  - old, unpinned sessions are recommended and selected by default;
  - recent sessions remain available but are not selected automatically;
  - pinned sessions remain available but are not selected automatically.
- Show measured worktree disk usage when available.
- Allow users to select additional recent or pinned sessions intentionally.
- Keep active, running, archived, and shared-worktree sessions out of the cleanup list.
- Explain when no worktrees are eligible instead of silently doing nothing.

The automatic prompt should continue to appear only at the unique-worktree threshold and only when at least one recommended old session exists.

Related implementation: an earlier issue

title: Retain full Claude shell output in Agent Host chat sessions
description:

- Attach an exited non-PTY terminal resource so the existing card shows its preview and **Open Full Output (Read-Only)** live and after restore, without keeping a terminal alive.

title: Agent Host: send_message should replace its unacknowledged queued message with an up-to-date one
description:
When one session messages another with `send_message` and the target chat is busy, every call adds another queued message. If the sender follows up before the target has started the first one, the target ends up with a stack of separate, unacknowledged messages from the same sender. Each becomes its own turn, and the earlier ones are usually out of date by the time they run.

## Proposal

When sessions talk to each other, the sender should read the most up-to-date state and keep one complete, current message in the target, not a stack of unread updates:

- The sender can read its own undelivered message, including any edits made to it while it waited, before sending again (for example, through `get_session_context`).
- Sending again before the target has started that message replaces it with one complete message that reflects the current state, not just what changed. The message keeps its ID, its place in the queue, and its model.
- The `send_message` result returns the text that was replaced, so the sender can tell whether anything it still needs was dropped.
- Once the target has started the message, which acknowledges it, the next message is queued as a new one.

title: Support expiring GitHub tokens with the offline_access scope
description:
GitHub sessions only expire today when they're brokered through Microsoft Entra (an earlier issue). Those sessions report `expiresAfter` and renew themselves before they run out. Ordinary GitHub OAuth sessions are stored in the keychain with no known expiry, and nothing ever renews them.

The GitHub Authentication extension should support expiring GitHub tokens for those sessions too, by requesting the `offline_access` scope. With `offline_access`, sign-in returns an access token that expires plus a refresh token. The extension would:

- store the refresh token next to the session
- report the access token's remaining lifetime through `expiresAfter`
- renew the access token before it expires, the same way Entra-brokered sessions renew today

The renewal path in `extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts` (`stillGood`) only handles transient Entra-brokered sessions. It will need to give persisted sessions their own expiry and branch on how a given session renews.

## Feature request

Support **Alt+click to open a link in an editor to the side of the current panel/editor group**, leaving the originating view visible.

## Proposed behavior

- Alt+click on a link opens its target in an editor group to the side of the group containing the clicked link.
- Keep the originating panel/view visible and unchanged.
- Reuse an appropriate adjacent editor group where possible instead of creating another split on every click.
- Preserve ordinary-click behavior.
- Propagate the side-opening intent through link handlers and contributed openers, including targets rendered as webview/custom editors, such as GitHub issue editors.
- Leave external-browser-only targets unaffected when they cannot be opened inside VS Code.

The placement should be relative to the view containing the clicked link, not an unrelated previously active editor group.

## Example

With a chat response containing a GitHub issue link visible, Alt+click the issue. The issue opens in an editor beside the chat, so both the response and the issue remain visible.

title: Let the integrated browser's toolbar be hidden, at least in compact floating windows
description:
## Summary

Compact mode for floating windows (since 1.100) removes tabs, breadcrumbs and
the status bar, so a floating window can show just one editor. For the
integrated browser, the browser's own toolbar (back, forward, reload, address,
actions) still takes about 40 px at the top. There is no setting, context key
or option to hide it.

## Use case

A small always-on-top window showing a page you work alongside: task
instructions, a checklist, a dashboard. At 420×640 the title bar and the
toolbar together take about 73 px, more than a tenth of the window. The page
is a local file the user opened on purpose; navigation controls are rarely
needed there.

## What exists today (source at tag 1.141.0, paths under `src/vs/`)

- The navigation bar is a toolbar widget that the browser editor mounts
  unconditionally (`workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/browserEditor.ts`
  L505–509). The widget contract (L264–269) has only `location`, `element` and
  `order`, with no visibility predicate. The navigation feature returns the
  widget with no condition (`features/browserNavigationFeatures.ts` L271).
- Nothing in the browser contribution reads the compact flag or the
  auxiliary-window context keys.
- `workbench.browser.showInTitleBar` controls the globe button in the window's
  title bar (`features/browserTabManagementFeatures.ts` L908–917), not this bar.
- Individual items can be hidden from the toolbar's overflow menu. an earlier issue
  (closed, shipped in 1.124) made more items

title: Offer Stop for detached background shells in Agent Host chats
description:
In Agent Host Copilot chats, the **Background Shells** pill lists both attached and detached background shells. Since an earlier issue, an attached shell can be stopped with **Stop Shell** in its details, but a detached one can't. Ending a detached dev server or watcher means finding and killing its process outside VS Code.

Offer **Stop Shell** for detached background shells too:

- Show Stop for a detached shell whenever the Copilot SDK can stop it: `session.rpc.tasks.list` reports the shell's process ID, and `session.rpc.tasks.cancel` stops it.
- Show a detached shell's details like an attached shell's: the command and its status in the same card, with Stop beside the command, even though there's no live output to show.
- Make Stop look the same in the editor window and the Agents window.

Stopping a detached shell shouldn't affect the chat's turn, since detached shells don't hold the turn open.
